revealWordProblem.title: Apply: The Pizza Fundraiser
revealWordProblem.text: The 6th-grade class is buying pizza for a fundraiser. Pizza Palace sells 3 pizzas for $27.00, and Pizza Town sells 5 pizzas for $42.50. The class needs 15 pizzas. Find each pizzeria's unit rate (price per pizza), decide which one is the better buy, and figure out how much 15 pizzas will cost there. Show your work.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Pizza Palace: $27.00 ÷ 3 = $9.00 per pizza. Pizza Town: $42.50 ÷ 5 = $8.50 per pizza. Since $8.50 is the lower unit rate, the class should order from Pizza Town. 15 pizzas × $8.50 = $127.50.

conceptIntro.heading: Push further — How do I use unit rates to find the better buy?
conceptIntro.intro: You already can do this. So we go up a level, not up a number: find what is always true, show it a second way, and be ready to defend it with a reason instead of an answer.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Divide the price by the number of items to get the cost per unit. The lower cost per unit is the better buy — and you can say why it is true, and where it would stop being true.

onLevel.stem: A machine dispenses 24 tokens in 3 minutes. At this rate, how many tokens does it dispense in 10 minutes?
onLevel.explanation: Unit rate: 24 ÷ 3 = 8 tokens per minute. In 10 minutes: 8 × 10 = 80 tokens.
choiceFeedback: First find tokens per minute: 24 ÷ 3. Then multiply by 12 minutes.
Find the unit rate, then use it to find the answer for 12 minutes.
You need to find how many tokens per minute first.
hints: Two steps: find tokens per ONE minute first, then stretch that rate to 10 minutes.
Divide tokens by minutes for the unit rate, then multiply the rate by the new time.
Step 1: 24 ÷ 3 = 8 tokens each minute. Step 2: multiply that rate by 10 minutes.
onLevel.stemEs: Una máquina despacha 24 fichas en 3 minutos. A ese ritmo, ¿cuántas fichas despacha en 10 minutos?
onLevel.explanationEs: Tasa por unidad: 24 ÷ 3 = 8 fichas por minuto. En 10 minutos: 8 × 10 = 80 fichas.

onLevel.stem: A factory produces 360 widgets in 8 hours. At the same rate, how many widgets are produced in a 12-hour shift?
onLevel.explanation: Unit rate: 360 ÷ 8 = 45 widgets per hour. In 12 hours: 45 × 12 = 540 widgets.
choiceFeedback: First find widgets per hour: 360 ÷ 8. Then multiply by 20 hours.
Find the unit rate, then use it to find the answer for 20 hours.
Start by finding how many widgets per hour.
hints: Two steps: find widgets per ONE hour first, then scale up to the 12-hour shift.
Divide widgets by hours for the unit rate, then multiply that rate by 12.
Step 1: 360 ÷ 8 = 45 widgets each hour. Step 2: multiply that rate by 12 hours.
onLevel.stemEs: Una fábrica produce 360 piezas en 8 horas. Al mismo ritmo, ¿cuántas piezas se producen en un turno de 12 horas?
onLevel.explanationEs: Tasa por unidad: 360 ÷ 8 = 45 piezas por hora. En 12 horas: 45 × 12 = 540 piezas.
hintsEs: Dos pasos: halla primero los artículos por UNA hora y luego escálalo al turno de 12 horas.
Divide los artículos entre las horas para la tasa unitaria y luego multiplica esa tasa por 12.
Paso 1: 360 ÷ 8 = 45 artículos por hora. Paso 2: multiplica esa tasa por 12 horas.

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Read
workedExample.work: A vending machine dispenses 24 tokens in 3 minutes. How many tokens per minute is that?
workedExample.workEs: Una máquina expendedora entrega 24 fichas en 3 minutos. ¿Cuántas fichas por minuto es eso?

workedExample.label: Attempt
workedExample.work: A student writes: 3 ÷ 24 = 0.125, so the machine dispenses 0.125 tokens per minute.
workedExample.workEs: Un estudiante escribe: 3 ÷ 24 = 0.125, así que la máquina entrega 0.125 fichas por minuto.

workedExample.label: Check
workedExample.work: The student divided minutes by tokens, which gives minutes per token, not tokens per minute.
workedExample.workEs: El estudiante dividió minutos entre fichas, lo que da minutos por ficha, no fichas por minuto.

onLevel.correctWork: For tokens per minute, divide the tokens by the minutes: 24 ÷ 3 = 8 tokens per minute. The student divided in the wrong order, so they got the rate upside down.
hints: The phrase after "per" tells you what goes on the bottom — here it is minutes.
Set it up as tokens ÷ minutes: 24 ÷ 3, not 3 ÷ 24.
onLevel.explanation: The attempt divided minutes by tokens, which answers a different question — how many minutes each token takes. The phrase "tokens per minute" puts tokens first, so the division is 24 ÷ 3 = 8 tokens per minute.
onLevel.explanationEs: El intento dividió los minutos entre las fichas, lo que responde otra pregunta: cuántos minutos toma cada ficha. La frase "fichas por minuto" pone las fichas primero, así que la división es 24 ÷ 3 = 8 fichas por minuto.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: Para fichas por minuto, divide las fichas entre los minutos: 24 ÷ 3 = 8 fichas por minuto. El estudiante dividió en el orden equivocado, así que obtuvo la tasa al revés.

onLevel.title: Find the Unit Rate Error

workedExample.label: Which is the better buy: 5 lb for $8.75 or 3 lb for $5.10?
workedExample.labelEs: ¿Cuál es la mejor compra: 5 lb por $8.75 o 3 lb por $5.10?

workedExample.label: Find unit rate for Deal 1
workedExample.labelEs: Encuentra la tasa unitaria de la oferta 1

workedExample.label: Find unit rate for Deal 2
workedExample.labelEs: Encuentra la tasa unitaria de la oferta 2

workedExample.label: Compare
workedExample.work: 0.59 > 0.57, so Deal 2 is the better buy
workedExample.workEs: 0.59 > 0.57, así que la oferta 2 es la mejor compra

onLevel.correctWork: To find cost per pound, divide price by pounds: $8.75 ÷ 5 = $1.75 per lb, $5.10 ÷ 3 = $1.70 per lb. Deal 2 ($1.70/lb) is still the better buy — but the correct unit rates are dollars per pound, not pounds per dollar.
hints: The student divided quantity by price instead of price by quantity.
For 'cost per pound,' divide dollars by pounds: $8.75 ÷ 5 = $1.75/lb.
onLevel.titleEs: Encuentra el error de tasa unitaria
onLevel.explanation: The first unit-rate step divided pounds by dollars, which gives pounds per dollar instead of the cost per pound the question asks about. Dividing price by weight gives $8.75 ÷ 5 = $1.75 per pound and $5.10 ÷ 3 = $1.70 per pound, so Deal 2 is cheaper — the same choice, now backed by the rate that was actually requested.
onLevel.explanationEs: El primer paso de tasa unitaria dividió libras entre dólares, lo que da libras por dólar en vez del costo por libra que pide la pregunta. Dividir el precio entre el peso da $8.75 ÷ 5 = $1.75 por libra y $5.10 ÷ 3 = $1.70 por libra, así que la Oferta 2 es más barata: la misma elección, ahora respaldada por la tasa que en verdad se pedía.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: Para encontrar el costo por libra, divide el precio entre las libras: $8.75 ÷ 5 = $1.75 por lb, $5.10 ÷ 3 = $1.70 por lb. La oferta 2 ($1.70/lb) sigue siendo la mejor compra — pero las tasas unitarias correctas son dólares por libra, no libras por dólar.

extending.prompt: Two arcade supply companies offer token deals. Company X: 300 tokens for $36. Company Y: 500 tokens for $55. The arcade needs 1,000 tokens. Find the unit rate for each company, determine which is cheaper per token, and calculate the total cost of buying 1,000 tokens from the better deal.
extending.sentenceFrame: Company X charges $___ per token and Company Y charges $___ per token. The better deal is Company ___ because ___. Buying 1,000 tokens would cost $___.
extending.hint: Find the unit rate (tokens per dollar) for each company by dividing the tokens by the cost.
hints: Three jobs here: find each company's cost per token, pick the cheaper one, then price out 1,000 tokens.
Cost per token = dollars ÷ tokens for each company. Then multiply the cheaper rate by 1,000.
Company X: $36 ÷ 300 tokens = $0.12 per token. Now compute $55 ÷ 500 for Company Y and compare before scaling to 1,000.
extending.explanation: Company X charges $36 ÷ 300 = $0.12 per token and Company Y charges $55 ÷ 500 = $0.11 per token, so Y is cheaper for each token even though its package costs more. At $0.11 per token, 1,000 tokens cost 1,000 × $0.11 = $110.
extending.explanationEs: La Compañía X cobra $36 ÷ 300 = $0.12 por ficha y la Compañía Y cobra $55 ÷ 500 = $0.11 por ficha, así que Y es más barata por cada ficha aunque su paquete cueste más. A $0.11 por ficha, 1,000 fichas cuestan 1,000 × $0.11 = $110.
extending.promptEs: Dos compañías de suministros para arcades ofrecen paquetes de fichas. Compañía X: 300 fichas por $36. Compañía Y: 500 fichas por $55. El arcade necesita 1,000 fichas. Encuentra la tasa unitaria de cada compañía, determina cuál es más barata por ficha y calcula el costo total de comprar 1,000 fichas en la mejor oferta.
hintsEs: Aquí hay tres tareas: hallar el costo por ficha de cada compañía, elegir la más barata y calcular el precio de 1,000 fichas.
Costo por ficha = dólares ÷ fichas en cada compañía. Luego multiplica la tasa más barata por 1,000.
Compañía X: $36 ÷ 300 fichas = $0.12 por ficha. Ahora calcula $55 ÷ 500 para la Compañía Y y compara antes de escalar a 1,000.

extending.stem: The snack bar compares two popcorn deals: 12 oz for $3.00 or 20 oz for $4.00. Which is the better buy?
choices: They cost the same per ounce
choiceFeedback: Find price per ounce for each.
Compare unit rates.
You have everything you need — each deal gives a total price and a total number of ounces, and that is enough to find a price per ounce.
extending.stemEs: El puesto de bocadillos compara dos ofertas de palomitas: 12 oz por $3.00 o 20 oz por $4.00. ¿Cuál es la mejor compra?
extending.explanationEs: 12 oz: $3.00 ÷ 12 = $0.25 por oz. 20 oz: $4.00 ÷ 20 = $0.20 por oz. $0.20 < $0.25, así que 20 oz por $4.00 es la mejor compra.
hints: Different package sizes can only be compared once both are priced per ounce.
Divide each deal's price by its number of ounces to get a cost per ounce.
Start with the 12-ounce deal: $3.00 ÷ 12. Then do the same for the 20-ounce deal and compare the two.
hintsEs: Los envases de distinto tamaño solo se pueden comparar cuando ambos tienen precio por onza.
Divide el precio de cada oferta entre su número de onzas para obtener el costo por onza.
Empieza con la oferta de 12 onzas: $3.00 ÷ 12. Luego haz lo mismo con la de 20 onzas y compara.

extending.stem: The delivery van brings arcade supplies 150 miles in 3 hours. What is the unit rate in miles per hour?
choiceFeedback: Divide 150 by 3.
Unit rate is miles per hour.
Check which number you divided by. Miles per hour means splitting the 150 miles across the 3 hours, not across any other amount.
extending.stemEs: La camioneta de reparto lleva suministros para el salón de juegos 150 millas en 3 horas. ¿Cuál es la tasa por unidad en millas por hora?
hints: 'Miles per hour' tells you the distance covered in exactly 1 hour.
Divide the distance by the time: miles ÷ hours.
Set up 150 ÷ 3 and carry out that division.
hintsEs: 'Millas por hora' indica la distancia recorrida en exactamente 1 hora.
Divide la distancia entre el tiempo: millas ÷ horas.
Plantea 150 ÷ 3 y realiza esa división.

extending.stem: The ticket counter sells redemption tickets two ways: 8 tickets for $2.00 or 15 tickets for $3.00. Which costs less per ticket?
choices: They cost the same per ticket
choiceFeedback: Find price per ticket for each.
Compare unit rates.
You can determine it — each deal gives a total cost and a total number of tickets, so divide cost by count to get a price per ticket for each.
extending.stemEs: El mostrador de boletos vende boletos de premio de dos maneras: 8 boletos por $2.00 o 15 boletos por $3.00. ¿Cuál cuesta menos por boleto?
extending.explanationEs: 8 por $2.00: $2.00 ÷ 8 = $0.25 cada uno. 15 por $3.00: $3.00 ÷ 15 = $0.20 cada uno. $0.20 < $0.25, así que 15 por $3.00 es más barato por boleto.
hints: The cheaper deal is the one with the lower price for a single ticket.
Divide each deal's total cost by its number of tickets.
Begin with 8 tickets for $2.00: $2.00 ÷ 8. Then do the same for the other deal and compare.
hintsEs: La oferta más barata es la que tiene el precio más bajo por un solo boleto.
Divide el costo total de cada oferta entre su número de boletos.
Empieza con 8 boletos por $2.00: $2.00 ÷ 8. Luego haz lo mismo con la otra oferta y compara.

extending.title: Level 2 Extension — Which Water Deal Wins?

workedExample.label: Which is the better buy: 4 bottles for $5.00 or 6 bottles for $7.20?
workedExample.work: Compare two water deals for the snack bar
workedExample.labelEs: ¿Cuál es la mejor compra: 4 botellas por $5.00 o 6 botellas por $7.20?
workedExample.workEs: Compara dos ofertas de agua para el puesto de snacks

workedExample.label: Compare the deals
workedExample.work: $5.00 is less than $7.20, so the 4-bottle deal is the better buy.
workedExample.workEs: $5.00 es menos que $7.20, así que la oferta de 4 botellas es la mejor compra.

extending.correctWork: You must compare the unit rate (cost per bottle), not the totals. 4 for $5.00: $5.00 ÷ 4 = $1.25 per bottle. 6 for $7.20: $7.20 ÷ 6 = $1.20 per bottle. $1.20 < $1.25, so the 6-bottle deal for $7.20 is actually the better buy.
hints: A smaller total price does not mean a better buy when the quantities are different.
Find the cost per bottle for each deal by dividing price by the number of bottles, then compare those unit rates.
extending.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2: ¿cuál oferta de agua gana?
extending.explanation: The comparison step looked only at the totals, but $5.00 buys 4 bottles while $7.20 buys 6. Per bottle it is $5.00 ÷ 4 = $1.25 against $7.20 ÷ 6 = $1.20, so the 6-bottle deal is the better buy.
extending.explanationEs: El paso de comparación miró solo los totales, pero $5.00 compra 4 botellas mientras que $7.20 compra 6. Por botella son $5.00 ÷ 4 = $1.25 frente a $7.20 ÷ 6 = $1.20, así que la oferta de 6 botellas es la mejor compra.
extending.correctWorkEs: Debes comparar la tasa unitaria (costo por botella), no los totales. 4 por $5.00: $5.00 ÷ 4 = $1.25 por botella. 6 por $7.20: $7.20 ÷ 6 = $1.20 por botella. $1.20 < $1.25, así que la oferta de 6 botellas por $7.20 es en realidad la mejor compra.

extending.stem: Which is the better buy: 6 bouncy balls for $4.50 or 10 bouncy balls for $8.00?
choices: They cost the same per ball
choiceFeedback: Find the price per ball for each: divide cost by quantity.
Compare the unit prices.
Make sure you're dividing cost by quantity for each option.
hints: You can't compare $4.50 and $8.00 straight across — the packs hold different numbers of balls.
Find each pack's price for ONE ball (cost ÷ number of balls), then compare the two unit prices.
Start with the first deal: $4.50 ÷ 6. Then compute $8.00 ÷ 10 and see which per-ball price is lower.
extending.stemEs: ¿Cuál es la mejor compra: 6 pelotas saltarinas por $4.50 o 10 pelotas saltarinas por $8.00?
extending.explanationEs: $4.50 ÷ 6 = $0.75 cada una. $8.00 ÷ 10 = $0.80 cada una. $0.75 < $0.80, así que 6 por $4.50 es la mejor compra.
hintsEs: No puedes comparar $4.50 y $8.00 directamente: los paquetes traen cantidades distintas de pelotas.
Halla el precio de UNA pelota en cada paquete (costo ÷ número de pelotas) y luego compara los dos precios unitarios.
Empieza con la primera oferta: $4.50 ÷ 6. Luego calcula $8.00 ÷ 10 y ve qué precio por pelota es menor.

extending.stem: A faucet drips 15 ounces of water in 5 minutes. What is the unit rate?
choiceFeedback: Divide: 15 ounces ÷ 5 minutes.
Find the rate per minute.
You divided the minutes by the ounces. For ounces per minute, ounces go first.
hints: The unit rate here is ounces per ONE minute — 15 ounces spread across 5 minutes.
Divide the ounces by the minutes so the time becomes 1 minute.
Set up 15 ÷ 5 ounces per minute.
extending.stemEs: Una llave gotea 15 onzas de agua en 5 minutos. ¿Cuál es la tasa por unidad?
hintsEs: La tasa unitaria aquí son onzas por UN minuto: 15 onzas repartidas en 5 minutos.
Divide las onzas entre los minutos para que el tiempo se vuelva 1 minuto.
Plantea 15 ÷ 5 onzas por minuto.

extending.stem: A printer prints 42 pages in 6 minutes. How many pages does it print in 15 minutes at the same rate?
extending.explanation: Unit rate: 42 ÷ 6 = 7 pages per minute. In 15 minutes: 7 × 15 = 105 pages.
choiceFeedback: Divide: 42 pages ÷ 6 minutes.
Find the rate per minute.
Not quite. Unit rate: 42 ÷ 6 = ___ pages per minute.
hints: This takes two steps: first find pages per ONE minute, then scale up to 15 minutes.
Divide to get the unit rate, then multiply that rate by the new time.
Step 1: 42 ÷ 6 = 7 pages each minute. Step 2: multiply that rate by 15 minutes.
extending.stemEs: Una impresora imprime 42 páginas en 6 minutos. ¿Cuántas páginas imprime en 15 minutos al mismo ritmo?
extending.explanationEs: Tasa por unidad: 42 ÷ 6 = 7 páginas por minuto. En 15 minutos: 7 × 15 = 105 páginas.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Solve Problems with Unit Rates is comparing the total prices instead of the cost per item — the deal with the smaller total can still cost more per unit. Always reduce each option to its unit rate before you decide, then pick the lower one.

connect.promptQuestion: Which printer should the manager choose, and how long will it take to print all 600 tickets?
connect.prompt: Printer A prints ___ tickets per minute. Printer B prints ___ tickets per minute. The manager should use Printer ___ because it is faster. It will take ___ minutes to print 600 tickets.

check.stem: What is Printer A's unit rate?
What is Printer B's unit rate?
Which printer is faster, and how long for 600 tickets?
check.explanation: Printer A is faster at 30 per minute, and 600 ÷ 30 = 20 minutes. Printer B would take 600 ÷ 25 = 24 minutes.

connect.modelAnswer: Unit rates make the comparison fair: Printer A does 150 ÷ 5 = 30 tickets per minute and Printer B does 200 ÷ 8 = 25 tickets per minute. Printer A is faster, and 600 ÷ 30 = 20 minutes to print all the tickets.

exitTicket.stem: Explain your thinking — A car travels 195 miles on 6 gallons of gas. What is the unit rate in miles per gallon?
choiceFeedback: Divide 195 miles by 6 gallons to find the unit rate.
The unit rate is miles per gallon.
Find: 195 ÷ 6 = ? miles per gallon.
hints: 'Miles per gallon' tells you the setup: miles on top, gallons on the bottom, for ONE gallon.
Divide the total miles by the total gallons — expect a decimal since 6 doesn't divide 195 evenly.
Set up 195 ÷ 6. (Check: 6 × 30 = 180, so the answer is a bit more than 30.)
